A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from FIG to SNaRe. Their main text, tables, figures, prompt illustrations, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot and few-shot experiments, component ablations, human evaluation, and additional analyses in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds multilingual evaluation, comparisons with newer LLMs, and an unlabeled-data sensitivity study.

M1.justification: Scout, Narrator, and Refiner correspond to FIG’s existing trigger extraction/filtering, conditioned passage generation, and missing-event refinement stages. Sampling, normalization, and downstream training remain equivalent. Corrected prompt illustrations document the already-described procedure; the multilingual downstream model is an evaluation configuration.

E1.justification: v2 adds Arabic and Chinese ACE evaluation to the retained ACE, SPEED, and GENIA coverage (Section 6.3, Table 2). Table 10 documents the additional multilingual training and test data. These additions substantially extend the represented languages.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 adds six ACE direct-inference comparators: Llama3.3-70B, Qwen2.5-72B, GPT4o-mini, GPT4o, QwQ-32B, and Deepseek-R1-L3-70B. This substantially expands comparison to newer and reasoning-oriented models. The earlier STAR, Weak Sup, and other comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The new multilingual experiments use TagPrime with XLM-RoBERTa-large, whereas the retained English experiments use DEGREE with BART-large. Appendix D.4 also introduces ACE evaluations using 20% and 5% of the unlabeled training pool with Llama3-70B. Existing experimental settings and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.4 and Table 18 add a focused sensitivity study of available unlabeled data. This differs from the retained Figure 5 study varying generated training examples. Earlier component ablations, data mixing, domain-prompt experiments, fine-tuning, human evaluation, and qualitative analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experimental results are averaged over three runs. Neither introduces seed information, dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The plots retain the same uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds multilingual, newer-LLM, and reduced-unlabeled-data results in Tables 2, 4, and 18. For example, Arabic Tri-C is 33.6/44.0 with Llama3-8B/70B; at 5% ACE unlabeled data, SNaRe scores 51.2 versus Weak Sup’s 44.9. These are newly evaluated settings. Table 1 and matched earlier tables and plots retain their scores.

T1.justification: The ED definitions, low-resource assumptions, and basic dataset notation retain equivalent meaning. Neither version supplies theoretical results or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: Multilingual generation moves from future work in v1’s conclusion to a demonstrated contribution in v2’s abstract, introduction, and conclusion, including claimed gains of 4–20 F1 points. The central claims about reducing label noise and domain drift remain, now presented through the renamed three-stage framework.

C2.justification: v2 interprets higher trigger overlap primarily as reduced domain drift rather than better annotation precision, and hypothesizes that larger external corpora yield cleaner triggers. It removes v1’s generation-versus-reasoning scaling discussion, emphasizes domain alignment from fine-tuning, and discusses applicability with scarce unlabeled data. The principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 corrects the swapped extraction/generation prompt illustrations and supplies a full-ontology structured Refiner prompt. It clarifies the Scout ablation, adds multilingual split statistics and Curator usage, and promises data release upon acceptance. Retained hyperparameters are unchanged, while v1’s explicit uniform-sampling statement is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Song et al. on domain knowledge, Ding et al. on LLM annotation, TagPrime, XLM-R, and Curator, while removing Kumar et al. and Meng et al. The discussion emphasizes domain-aware generation but retains its principal relationship to STAR and weak supervision.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and methodology are substantially rewritten around Scout, Narrator, and Refiner. Related work moves from Section 7 to Section 3, the separate forward/inverse background is replaced with integrated motivation, and the method receives component subsections. Results discussion is also condensed and reorganized.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are extensively redrawn with concrete examples. v2 adds Tables 2, 4, and 18 and expands the data-statistics table. Prompt Figures 7–9 are corrected or revised and relocated. Figure 4’s ExGen legend becomes SNaRe without changing its curves. The new multilingual Table 2 has a mismatched caption describing powerful-LLM comparisons.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical case by testing language generality, comparison against newer reasoning models, and sensitivity to the required unlabeled-data supply (Tables 2, 4, and 18). These address important questions untested in v1. Corrected prompt illustrations also improve reproducibility. The gains outweigh the mismatched Table 2 caption and limited training detail for the new multilingual experiments; retained benchmark scores are unchanged.
